# qthid-fcd-controller

**Sets frequency and gain on a FUNcube Dongle**

- **Version recorded:** 4.1
- **Categories:** `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://oz9aec.net/radios/funcube-dongle/updated-fcdctl-for-the-funcube-dongle-pro-and-pro>

## What it does

A small control panel for the FUNcube Dongle Pro and Pro+: it sets the tuning frequency, the LNA and mixer gains, the filter selections and the IQ correction, all of which the dongle exposes over USB HID rather than through its audio interface.

## Why you would want it

The FUNcube presents itself as a sound card, so audio software can read its samples but has no way to tune it. This is the other half. Without something like it the dongle sits wherever it was last set.

## Before it will work

A FUNcube Dongle, and permission to open its HID device -- a udev rule, since HID access is not granted to ordinary users by default.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install qthid-fcd-controller --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `qthid-fcd-controller`

## Known problems

Pro and Pro+ have different frequency coverage and different gain controls, and a control that does nothing usually means the wrong model assumption rather than a fault. This catalog also carries `gr-funcube` for the GNU Radio path; the two do not conflict but only one should be holding the device at a time.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
